name: Jaipur
tagline: The pink city of Rajput palaces, bazaars and forts.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: The cool, clear October-to-February window is Jaipur's season, crowned by the January literature festival. Avoid the scorching summer and soft monsoon light.

ourTake.lede: Jaipur repays slowing down; the palaces are best in the first two hours after opening, and the walled Pink City is a morning proposition before the heat and crowds. Don't buy the tourist-trap gem 'factory' visits; do seek out the genuine block-printers, blue-pottery and jewellery ateliers. Stay in a restored haveli or palace hotel rather than a generic property, because here the lodging is half the experience.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the pink city's palaces, forts and the polish of the Golden Triangle.
ourTake.skipIf: You want nature or quiet; Jaipur is grand, busy and steeped in commerce.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

Condé Nast Traveller, Favourite Indian Leisure Hotel

credentials: Marriott Luxury Collection
MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: A haveli-inspired Luxury Collection house, courtyards and step-wells, minutes from the old city.

items.name: Samode Haveli
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Readers' Travel Awards 2025, Top 20 Hotels in India
items.description: A 225-year-old family haveli inside the old walls, frescoed, romantic, and quietly grand.

items.name: Fairmont Jaipur
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India Readers' Travel Awards 2025, recognised
Travel + Leisure India, Best Sustainable Hotel (2024)
items.description: A palatial modern fort of a resort on the road to Amber, grand-scale Rajput theatre.

items.name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort) & the Sheesh Mahal
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hill Forts of Rajasthan (Amer, 2013)
items.description: The Kachhwaha capital before Jaipur existed: honey-coloured sandstone and marble rising off a hillside, with the Sheesh Mahal's mirror-work catching a single flame into a thousand. Come at 8am before the crowds, and ask your hotel to arrange a private guided walk of the Diwan-e-Khas and Sukh Niwas before the guides start herding.

items.name: The ascent to Amber, jeep, not elephant
items.description: The postcard is the caparisoned elephant climbing to the Suraj Pol, but the welfare questions are real and increasingly hard to ignore. The dignified choice for a multi-gen group is the open 4WD jeep up the ramp, or better still a morning at a walk-alongside sanctuary like Elefantastic near the fort where children meet the elephants on their own terms.

items.name: City Palace & Chandra Mahal
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Jaipur City (2019)
items.description: Still the working home of the Jaipur royal family, which is exactly why the private Chandra Mahal tour matters: you climb through the seven-storey palace the public never sees, ending on the peacock-painted upper floors with a butler and a view over the whole pink grid. The Baradari courtyard is where you take tea between the Pritam Niwas Chowk's four seasonal gates.

items.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Jaipur City (2019)
items.description: The 953-window honeycomb screen the royal women watched the street from, unseen. Everyone photographs the facade from the coffee shop across Badi Chaupar; far fewer go inside and up to the top-floor jharokhas for the light through pink lattice. Best in the first hour of morning sun.

items.name: Jantar Mantar observatory
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (2010)
items.description: Sawai Jai Singh II's obsession made stone: nineteen giant astronomical instruments, including the world's largest sundial, that still tell the time to the second. It reads as sculpture to the eye and as pure science to the mind, a rare thing to hand a curious teenager. Take the licensed guide; the instruments are meaningless without one.

items.name: Nahargarh Fort at sunset
items.description: The 'abode of tigers' on the ridge, and the finest sunset seat in Jaipur, the whole pink grid laid out below as the light goes gold. Time it so you drift up in the late afternoon, walk the Madhavendra Bhawan's linked queens' apartments, and stay for a drink at Padao as the city lamps come on.

items.name: Jaigarh Fort & the Jaivana cannon
items.description: The muscular military fort above Amber, connected by subterranean passage, and home of Jaivana, one of the largest wheeled cannons ever cast, and never fired in anger. Less about palaces, more about engineering: water-harvesting tanks, ramparts, the old foundry. A good counterpoint for the men and boys after a morning of mirror-work.

items.name: Jal Mahal (Water Palace)
items.description: The palace that appears to float on Man Sagar Lake, four of its five storeys submerged. You don't go in, you stop on the lakeshore at dusk when the light softens and migratory birds settle, a five-minute pause on the way to or from Amber that is pure Rajput romance.

items.name: Albert Hall Museum
items.description: Rajasthan's oldest museum, a fantastical Indo-Saracenic pile by Samuel Swinton Jacob, floodlit gold after dark. Inside: Mughal miniatures, an Egyptian mummy, and the famous carpet collection. Worth the visit for the building alone, and the lit-up evening view from Ram Niwas Garden is a set piece.

items.name: Amrapali Museum of jewellery
items.description: A jeweller's private obsession made public: some 4,000 pieces of Indian tribal and antique silver, gold and adornment across two floors, curated with a connoisseur's eye. For anyone shopping the trousseau or simply in love with Indian craft, it recalibrates what 'good' looks like before you buy a thing.

items.name: Johari Bazaar, the jewellers' street
items.description: The historic gem and jewellery bazaar, and the front door to Jaipur's kundan, meenakari and polki trade. The real business happens in the family workshops in the lanes behind, where a discreet introduction, best arranged through your hotel or advisor, gets you sitting down with a house that has cut stones for generations, not a shopfront.

items.name: Gem Palace
items.description: Jaipur's most storied jewellery house, jewellers to maharajas and, over the years, to a long list of international collectors. Go for the private viewing upstairs rather than the counter: enamelled Mughal-revival pieces and old-cut diamonds brought out one tray at a time over tea. The benchmark against which the rest of the city is judged.

items.name: Bapu Bazaar & Nehru Bazaar
items.description: The textile heart of the walled city: bolts of Bandhani and Leheriya tie-dye, Sanganeri block-print by the metre, mojari and jutti leatherwork. This is where you kit out the home and the trousseau in colour, send a member of staff or your advisor ahead to hold aside the good pieces so the family isn't bargaining in the heat.

items.name: Tripolia Bazaar, lac bangles
items.description: Below the triple-arched Tripolia gate, the lane of lac-bangle makers where you watch artisans work molten lac over a flame and set it with mirror and stone. A small, tactile, wonderfully un-touristy stop for a bride's chooda or simply to see a living craft that hasn't moved buildings in generations.

items.name: Blue pottery ateliers (Kripal Kumbh & the Sanganeri Gate lanes)
items.description: Jaipur's signature cobalt-and-white glazed ware, a Persian craft the city made its own, no potter's clay in it at all, but quartz. Kripal Singh Shekhawat's studio kept the art alive; a visit to a working atelier lets you commission tiles or a dinner service for the house rather than buy off a shelf.

items.name: Bagru, hand block-printing village
items.description: The village behind the fabric: earthy dabu mud-resist and natural indigo printed by hand, the old way, on long courtyards of drying cotton. A private half-day here, carving a block, dipping the indigo, lunch with a printing family, is the sort of quiet, rooted experience that stays with children long after a fort blurs.

items.name: Sanganer, the fine block-print & handmade paper town
items.description: Bagru's more delicate cousin: fine Sanganeri florals on white grounds, plus the handmade-paper mills that supply the world. Closer to the city than Bagru and easily paired with a workshop visit, it's the source many of the boutique labels quietly buy from.

items.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
items.description: A restored 16th-century pink-sandstone haveli near Amber, turned into a jewel of a museum devoted to hand block-printing, living demonstrations of carving and printing, and a shop that sets the standard. A civilised, air-cooled counterpoint to the fort, and it won a UNESCO cultural-conservation award for the restoration.

items.name: Panna Meena ka Kund stepwell
items.description: The perfectly symmetrical criss-cross stairway stepwell a short walk from Amber Fort, a 16th-century community tank that is pure geometry, and blessedly cool. Go early, before the influencer crowd; it pairs naturally with a morning at the fort and the Anokhi haveli.

items.name: Galtaji (the Monkey Temple)
items.description: A temple complex tucked into a pink-rock gorge, with seven sacred water tanks fed by a natural spring and, yes, a resident troop of macaques. Come at golden hour for the ridge-top Sun Temple view over the city, atmospheric, a little wild, and genuinely off most first-time itineraries.

items.name: Patrika Gate
items.description: The most photographed modern gateway in the city: a run of arches painted end to end with Rajasthan's regions and motifs, opening onto Asia's largest circular garden. Not old, but a genuine crowd-pleaser and a guaranteed portrait for the family album, go at first light to have the colonnade to yourselves.

items.name: Sisodia Rani Garden & Palace
items.description: The tiered Mughal-style pleasure garden a maharaja built for his queen, with painted pavilions, fountains and terraces climbing the hillside. A calm, green half-hour away from the walled-city crush, lovely in the soft light of late afternoon and rarely crowded.

items.name: Kanak Vrindavan garden & temple
items.description: A restored Krishna garden-and-temple at the foot of the Nahargarh hills on the road to Amber, carved marble columns, lattices and terraces, the sort of serene, film-set setting locals use for celebrations. An easy, pretty pause to fold into the Amber run.

items.name: Jawahar Kala Kendra
items.description: Charles Correa's masterwork of an arts centre, its nine-square plan a modern echo of Jaipur's own mandala city grid. Galleries, theatres and a good café inside a building that architects fly in to see, the cultured, contemporary side of a city usually pitched as pure heritage.

items.name: Birla Mandir (Lakshmi Narayan Temple)
items.description: A serene modern temple in white Makrana marble below the Moti Dungri fort, glowing when floodlit after dark. Quiet, cool and beautifully carved, a peaceful, veg-and-Jain-friendly stop that families of every generation take to.

items.name: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple
items.description: Jaipur's most beloved Ganesh shrine, below a private Scottish-castle-style palace on the hill, thronged with the faithful especially on Wednesdays. A short, meaningful darshan for those who want the living-faith Jaipur, not just the museum one.

items.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
items.description: The Krishna temple at the heart of the City Palace gardens, its deity brought from Vrindavan by the city's founder, where thousands gather for the aartis through the day. Time your City Palace visit around one of the seven daily darshans for something the guidebook photos can't convey.

items.name: 1135 AD at Amber Fort, royal dining
items.description: Dinner inside the fort itself, in candlelit halls hung with gilt and glass, on recipes once guarded by the palace kitchens. Book the private Sheesh Mahal room and let them build a Rajasthani thali; it turns a sightseeing day into an occasion, and the vegetarian menu is deep and effortless.

items.name: Suvarna Mahal at Rambagh Palace
items.description: The old Rambagh banqueting hall, frescoed, chandeliered, palatial, serving the royal cuisines of Rajasthan, Awadh, Punjab and Hyderabad off gold-rimmed plates. Even if you're not staying at the Taj's flagship palace hotel, dinner here (and a Polo Bar nightcap) is the grandest table in the city.

items.name: High tea at SUJÁN Rajmahal Palace
items.description: The former royal guest palace, reborn in bold heritage-print interiors, where afternoon tea is served on the lawns among portraits of the family who hosted Jackie Kennedy and the Queen here. A witty, intimate, only-in-Jaipur way to spend a slow afternoon between forts.

items.name: Pink City heritage walk at dawn
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Jaipur City (2019)
items.description: The old city wakes slowly, flower sellers, temple bells, the wholesale markets before the shutters go up, and a private guided walk through the chowkris and hidden havelis at first light is the single best way to read Jai Singh's planned grid. Cool, quiet, and endlessly photogenic.

items.name: A private Rajasthani cooking session
items.description: Hands in the masala: a home or poolside masterclass in dal-baati-churma, gatte ki sabzi and the sweets, almost entirely vegetarian and Jain-adaptable by default. The palace hotels (SUJÁN Rajmahal, Rambagh) run polished versions; a home kitchen with a local cook is the warmer, more personal one for a family.

items.name: Sunrise hot-air balloon over Amer
items.description: Sky Waltz floats you up at first light over Amber Fort, the lakes and the ridge forts, the whole Kachhwaha landscape spread out gold beneath the basket. India's original licensed operator, a genuinely once-in-a-trip experience, and a spectacular treat for older children and grandparents alike.

items.name: Polo at Rambagh & the season
items.description: Jaipur is the spiritual home of Indian polo, and the winter season still draws the old sporting set to the grounds by Rambagh. Catch a match if the calendar aligns, or simply take a drink at the Polo Bar among the trophies and the famous walnut travelling bar, the city's most patrician afternoon.

items.name: Isarlat (Sargasuli) victory tower
items.description: The slender 1749 victory tower rising over Tripolia Bazaar, its spiral stair climbing to one of the few open rooftop views inside the walled city. A quiet, quirky ten-minute detour that puts the whole pink grid at your feet, and almost nobody bothers.

items.name: Central Park & the Statue Circle
items.description: Jaipur's green lung, ringed by a walking track, an enormous tricolour and rose gardens, with the white-marble statue of the astronomer-king Jai Singh II at its edge. A civilised early-morning walk for a family staying in the leafy C-Scheme quarter, before the heat.

items.name: Raj Mandir Cinema
items.description: The 'pride of Asia', a meringue-pink Art Moderne movie palace where the interiors are the real show and the audience cheers the star's first frame. Book the box seats for a Bollywood matinee; it's kitsch, joyous and utterly Jaipur, and children never forget it.

items.name: Jaipur Modern & the design boutiques of C-Scheme
items.description: The city's contemporary-design side: concept stores and ateliers like Jaipur Modern, Hot Pink and the Anokhi flagship, where Rajasthani craft is cut for a modern home and wardrobe. The considered, air-conditioned alternative to bazaar bargaining for those furnishing a house.

items.name: Studio visit to a miniature painter
items.description: Jaipur keeps the Rajput-Mughal miniature tradition alive, squirrel-hair brushes, stone pigments, gold leaf, a peacock painted on a grain of rice. A private studio sitting, arranged through your advisor, lets you commission a family piece and watch a craft measured in years of apprenticeship.

items.name: Chand Baori stepwell, Abhaneri (day trip)
items.description: One of India's deepest and most dramatic stepwells, thirteen storeys of dizzying, perfectly geometric steps, the one you've seen in films. About two hours out toward Agra, best folded into a chauffeured day with lunch, and a genuine jaw-drop for the whole family.

items.name: Samode Palace (day trip or overnight)
items.description: A 475-year-old palace of painted durbar halls and mirrored chambers, now a heritage hotel at the foot of the Aravallis. Come for a long, unhurried lunch and a wander through the Sheesh Mahal frescoes, or stay a night away from the city to bookend a Jaipur trip in perfect quiet.

items.name: Ranthambore National Park (extended day / overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hill Forts of Rajasthan (Ranthambore Fort, 2013)
items.description: The wild-tiger reserve within striking distance of Jaipur, best done as an overnight from a lodge like SUJÁN Sher Bagh with private naturalists and a dawn safari through the ruined-fort jungle. Not a half-day trip, but the natural-heritage crown on a Rajasthan itinerary for a family that wants more than forts.

items.name: Sunset drinks at a rooftop over the walled city
items.description: As the light drops, the pink grid glows and the rooftops fill, spots above Hawa Mahal and along the old city put the Palace of Winds and the Nahargarh ridge in one frame. A gentle, unstructured hour to close a day of forts, chai or something stronger in hand.

items.name: Bespoke perfume & attar at Sugandh Co / the ittar makers
items.description: Jaipur's old attar tradition, natural oil-based ittars of rose, khus, oudh and the monsoon-earth 'mitti', blended to order in tiny walled-city shops. A small, sensory, deeply personal thing to carry home, and a lovely gift to layer into the trousseau.

items.name: Suvarna Mahal
credentials: Inside Rambagh Palace, Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice 2025, No. 1 Hotel in India
items.description: Royal Indian dining on gold-plated tableware beneath Florentine ceilings, the grandest table in Jaipur.

items.name: Dining at The Oberoi Rajvilas
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Rajvilas, Travel + Leisure World's Best 2024, No. 1 Hotel in the World
items.description: Considered Rajasthani and international cooking in the most decorated hotel in the city, faultless, and framed by fort-walled gardens.

items.name: Bar Palladio
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, featured Jaipur restaurant
Featured in Architectural Digest & WSJ Magazine
items.description: Cobalt-blue Italian fantasy under tented canopies and mango trees, the chicest room in Jaipur.

items.name: Dining at SUJÁN Rajmahal Palace
credentials: Inside SUJÁN Rajmahal Palace, Relais & Châteaux; MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: Refined palace cooking amid the maison's fantastical wallpapers, a private, high-tea-to-dinner occasion.

items.name: Polo Bar
credentials: Inside Rambagh Palace, Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice 2025, No. 1 Hotel in India; MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: Rare whiskies and colonial-era charm amid polo memorabilia, the grandest nightcap in Jaipur.

items.name: Bar Palladio
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, featured Jaipur venue
Featured in Architectural Digest & WSJ Magazine
items.description: A cobalt-blue Italian dream under garden canopies, as much a scene as a drink.

plan.heading: 3 days in Jaipur, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Check into Rambagh Palace, the former Maharaja's residence, and take tea on the veranda.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The City Palace and Jantar Mantar observatory with a private guide, then the Hawa Mahal at dusk.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Suvarna Mahal within Rambagh, under its chandeliers and gold-leaf ceilings.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Early at Amber Fort before the crowds, up through the Ganesh Pol to the mirror hall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Anokhi's block-printing museum and the workshops of the old city, blue pottery, gemstones, textiles.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dine at the Rajput thali at 1135 AD inside Amber Fort, or Bar Palladio for its blue-and-white Italian rooms.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The stepwell at Panna Meena ka Kund and the Jal Mahal on the water, then Nahargarh Fort for the city view.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Shopping at Hot Pink and the antique dealers of Amrapali before an unhurried lunch.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final drink at the Polo Bar at Rambagh before the drive to the airport.

items.name: Walled Pink City
items.description: The historic heart of bazaars and palaces; best for those who want to be inside the atmosphere on foot.

items.name: Civil Lines / Rambagh area
items.description: Gracious, leafy and home to the grand palace hotels; suits travellers wanting calm and grandeur.

items.name: Amer / edge of the city
items.description: Near the fort and quieter, with boutique heritage stays; for those prioritising the forts over the bazaars.

events.name: Jaipur Literature Festival
events.note: The world's largest free literary festival, a genuine cultural draw that fills the city; book lodging far ahead.

events.name: Teej
events.note: A monsoon festival with a colourful royal procession honouring the goddess Parvati through the old city.

events.name: Gangaur
events.note: An 18-day festival ending in a grand ceremonial procession, one of Rajasthan's most photographed.

events.name: Diwali
events.note: Jaipur is famous for its illuminated markets and lit-up buildings at Diwali; among the best in India to witness.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in a heritage palace (Rambagh Palace, SUJAN Rajmahal, or the Oberoi Rajvilas just outside town); dress modestly for temples, and plan the forts for early morning to avoid heat and crowds.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive at Jaipur International Airport (JAI), a short and calm transfer by chauffeured car to the palace hotels within twenty to thirty minutes.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver, ideally with a knowledgeable guide, is how to see the forts and old city without friction.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Solid 4G/5G in the city and strong hotel wifi; an Indian eSIM or Jio/Airtel SIM is simple.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Indian rupee (INR); cards are accepted at hotels and larger shops, keep cash for bazaars, and tipping around ten percent is expected.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Oct-Mar is the fine window, cool and clear for the forts and palaces; Nov-Feb mornings can be genuinely cold. Avoid Apr-Jun, when desert heat pushes past 40C, and the humid Jul-Sep monsoon.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: From India: a short 1-2 hour hop from Delhi, or roughly 2 hours from Mumbai and Bengaluru, into Jaipur (JAI) on Vistara or IndiGo; many also drive the roughly 5 hours from Delhi. The airport is compact and close to town, so arrival is quick, but lounge choice is limited; a pre-booked chauffeur to your palace hotel is the smooth way in.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Routine vaccines plus Hepatitis A and typhoid advised; use sealed or filtered water. Jaipur is safe for careful travellers; the practical cautions are extreme pre-monsoon heat (Apr-Jun) and the usual attention to belongings in crowded bazaars and around the major forts.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Wonderfully easy; Rajasthan is a heartland of vegetarian and Jain cooking, and Jain thalis are standard. Try the classic dal-baati-churma and Rajasthani thali at places like Suvarna Mahal or a heritage-hotel kitchen for a refined vegetarian spread.
